title: Behold the Sure Foundation-stone
description: Behold the Sure Foundation-stone in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 118, part 3, headed “Christ the foundation of his church”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold the sure foun-da-tion stone Which God in Zi-on lays To build our heav-enly hopes up-on, And his e-ter-nal praise.

lines: To build our heavenly hopes upon,
Chosen of God, to sinners dear,
They trust their whole salvation here,
The foolish builders, scribe and priest,
Yet on this rock the church shall rest,
What tho' the gates of hell withstood,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
